newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil premiums drift, cold supports cargoes.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil premiums drift, cold supports cargoes.

text.p: NWE gas oil premiums drifted around unchanged in inactive business on Monday but cargo premiums won mild support from forecasts of colder U.S. and European weather, traders said.
"There's a hell of a lot of winter yet to come," one trader said. "I'm quite supportive of this market."
Benchmark Jan IPE futures closed up $8.75 at 222.75 a tonne on buying by funds and the cold forecasts.
Cash market volumes were minimal, with most activity focussed on planning or quietly running down positions and stocks before the Christmas and New Year holidays.
"It's absolutely dead," said a barge trader.
Bulls noted predictions by U.S. weather forecasters that the the U.S. Midwest and Northeast will have bouts of sharply below normal temperatures through year-end.
Barges of heating oil refinery grade traded at Jan IPE -$1 fob Rotterdam, around $1 easier, for second half December. Offers of low sulphur diesel French grade were Jan IPE +$11.
On cargoes, heating oil material into Hamburg was bid around Jan IPE +$5.50/6 with offers notionally around $7. Low sulphur diesel was around Jan +$13.50/15.
